## Change 2656 pushed — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2656

Not submitted; ticket left `in_progress`. The operator verifies votes and submits.

### AC1 — the violator no longer allocates into the shared root

`test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py` now routes through `run_nested_pytest`.
The `python -c` payload's `assert 'pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic' not in sys.modules` was
dropped, and that loses nothing: it ran before `pytest.main`, in an interpreter that had
imported only `sys`, so it could not fail. A fresh `python -m pytest` child IS the condition
the test names.

Proof, run under an explicit parent `--basetemp` so the module's children were the only thing
that could touch the shared root:

```
--- created ---   (none)
--- DELETED ---   (none)
child basetemps:  .bt/ac1/test_anthropic_auth_oracle_iso{0,1,2,3}/nested-pytest
```

4 passed. Pre-fix the same module created four roots and deleted four.

### AC2/AC3 — the guard, and the seeded defects

The guard no longer matches one argv shape. It classifies a sequence literal into three
spellings of one operation and applies the admission each can actually satisfy:

| spelling | detection | admitted by |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m pytest` | argv triple `(sys.executable, "-m", "pytest")` | the helper, or a reasoned marker |
| `python -c <payload naming pytest>` | `(sys.executable, "-c", payload)` where the payload's static text mentions pytest, resolved through the module's string bindings (the violator bound its payload to a local first) and through f-string literal parts | the helper, or a reasoned marker |
| bare `pytest` console script | argv[0] is `<anything> / "pytest"`, directly or via a local, through a `str()`/`os.fspath()` wrapper | an explicit `--basetemp` in the same literal, or a marker |

The console-script form gets the weaker admission on purpose: it *cannot* use the helper
(`python -m pytest` puts the repo root on the child's `sys.path` and destroys what those tests
reproduce), and the invariant being defended is the child's temp root, not the helper's
monopoly.

Defect seeding, in the real tree, one spelling at a time, watching
`test_the_launch_appears_only_in_the_helper`:

```
baseline (all fixed)                          PASS
seed 1: -c payload (the pre-fix violator)     FAIL
seed 2: console script, --basetemp removed    FAIL
seed 3: the -m triple (regression check)      FAIL
restored                                      PASS
```

Files were set aside by copy under `git rev-parse --git-path heldout`, per the move pattern in
tasteful-euhedral-bilby. No stash was used anywhere.

The pre-fix payload is also kept verbatim in the guard as `_PRE_FIX_VIOLATOR`, so a revert
stays a permanently checked defect rather than one checked once by hand.

### AC4 — the sweep and its dispositions

Scanned: every `*.py` under `tests/` (the guard's own tree walk is the sweep), plus a manual
grep over `tests/`, `scripts/` and `src/` for `pytest.main`, quoted `pytest`,
`Popen`/`check_output`/`check_call`, and every `"-c"` argv.

| site | spelling | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py:32` | `-c` payload, no basetemp | fixed here (AC1) |
| `test_tests_import_convention.py:97` | bare console script, NO basetemp | fixed here. Second violator, found by the widened guard; `--basetemp` added under `tmp_path` |
| `test_scripts_import_convention.py:154` | bare console script | already passes `--basetemp`; admitted unchanged |
| `test_mechanism_delta.py:440` | bare console script | already passes `--basetemp`; admitted unchanged |
| `test_error_handling_convention.py:125`, `workflow/test_terraform_plan_review_tools.py:300`, `workflow/test_map_fanout.py:294`, `interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:365` | in-process `pytest.main` | all four sit inside `if __name__ == "__main__":`, so they never run during a suite. Not flagged, deliberately |
| `test_ci_workflow_parity.py:1337` | `stub_bin / "pytest"` | a stub written to disk and put on `PATH`, never argv[0]. Correctly not flagged; verified |
| `test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py`, `test_repo_isolation_guard.py` | `pytester.runpytest*` | pytest owns their basetemp; already recorded as out of scope in `_nested_pytest.py` |
| `scripts/run_live_matrix.py:80`, `scripts/mutation_gate.py:579` | build a pytest argv | outside `tests/`, so outside this guard's tree walk. NOT covered, see below |

Zero false positives: every other `python -c` payload under `tests/` (about a dozen) stays
unflagged, and two negative-control tests pin that.

### What the guard still cannot see, stated rather than claimed away

- Anything outside `tests/`. `scripts/run_live_matrix.py` and `scripts/mutation_gate.py`
  construct pytest argvs; the tree walk is rooted at `tests/`. They are operator tooling
  rather than suite children, so they cannot prune a concurrent session's root the way a test
  can, but the guard does not check them and its root was not widened here.
- argv assembled incrementally (`cmd = [sys.executable]` then `cmd += ["-m", "pytest"]`).
  Detection is per sequence literal; no literal holds the triple. Not present in the tree today.
- A console script not at argv[0], e.g. `["env", "X=1", str(console_script), ...]`. Only argv[0]
  is checked. Not present today.
- A `-c` payload that reaches pytest only through an interpolated value, so no literal part of
  the f-string says "pytest". Not present today.

Each is a narrower gap than the one just closed, and each is listed so the next reader knows it
was a choice.

### Gates and checks

`make lint` rc=0; `make typecheck` rc=0 (762 files). Complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0
stale=16`; mechanism ratchet `new=0 increased=0`. No new mechanism: the change reshapes an
existing guard rather than adding one.

Verified with the BARE `pytest` console script throughout, not `python -m pytest`:
`test_tests_import_convention.py` + `test_scripts_import_convention.py` green, and the five
affected modules green (57 passed).

### One transient, recorded not chased

`test_scripts_import_convention.py::test_repro_module_passes_standalone` failed once inside a
four-module selection (child rc 1 while its own output said "3 passed"), then passed 4/4 on
re-run with the identical selection under `-p no:randomly`. That module is unmodified by this
change. The shape matches the same-family transient already noted in this ticket's description;
not investigated further here.
